title: Don't just say yes to your AI. All my characters had helmets instead of hair and I didn't notice
author: Dapper-Business5405
selftext:
Hi fellow AI devs (or maybe fellow sufferers 😂),

I want to share my experience with the idea "the AI does everything by itself anyway, and I only have to say yes".

In my game Kiosk Days, a 2D kiosk management game, I asked the AI to design my customers. Claude draws every sprite with Python code, pixel by pixel. After a few rounds where I always had something to improve, at some point I only said "yes, put it in the game" and I only looked at the detail I had told the AI last. But the AI drew the hair of the characters so that it actually looked like helmets. And I only noticed it a few days later.

It didn't break the game, because it was nothing that changes how it plays, but it kind of ruined the look. In the picture you see before (top) and after (bottom). The guy on the right really wears a hard hat 😄 

How do you do this? Do you always check everything down to the last pixel /codeline? When you add a new feature or fix a bug, do you only test that, or do you also do regular regression tests where you test everything again?

I always think i just have to write something and the AI will do it and it will be fine. But more and more I find out that game development with AI is (of course, and if you want to create no AI slop) also a lot of work and takes time, and most of all patience.

What are your experiences? And where do you draw the line: what do you still do or check yourself, and what do you just let the AI do?

  
And, in the end, I hope you’ll allow me a bit of self-promotion: The game is free on itch.io: [https://kigaro-games.itch.io/kiosk-days](https://kigaro-games.itch.io/kiosk-days)

And here are some screenshots: [https://imgur.com/a/fsyF54s](https://imgur.com/a/fsyF54s)

comments.author: deadmileage
comments.body: Haha, nice one. The AI tries to reuse what it can. If the first one had a cut like that, it will just try to get away with changing the color. It kinda makes sense

comments.author: GraniteBitGames
comments.body: lol yeah.  AI can do some amazing things but ultimatley you need to QC most things. So easy to get complacent on what's being produced. I always check, check and check again.  Doesn't mean I catch everything though either.

replies.author: Dapper-Business5405
replies.body: Yes, and that is the most important lesson for me. But I am wondering if you can set up an agent that does not know the game and test it. I mean, it would probably have missed the helmet thing, but for other things it might be helpful. It's like in real life: the developer is a bad tester.

replies.author: GraniteBitGames
replies.body: just give it rules. So if you don't want 'helmet hair', set a rule to say "Don't use helmets or other objects as hair and only use objects on the head when instructed." etc. then improve the rule as you go.

replies.author: Dapper-Business5405
replies.body: How do you manage your rules? I already have so many rules that I can't even remember them myself.

replies.author: GraniteBitGames
replies.body: could just prompt it to create a document containing the rules in memory.
